one_line: A shared live mathematics canvas where a student and AI tutor manipulate the same computed objects through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Provides an infinite math canvas spanning graphs, attention, geometry, matrices, and partitions, with attributed learner/tutor edits and shared undo history.
leverage_rationale: The core promise is shared structured state: agent edits use the same typed reducer and history as learner edits, enabling precise, visible, repeatable mathematical manipulation that ordinary UI driving would reproduce poorly.
leverage_evidence: Pitch states 48 native WebMCP tools and one shared undo history.
Transcript describes computed dependencies, tool-call glows, attribution, and undo of tutor edits.
Transcript says every tutor edit went through a registered tool and the student reached the same reducer.
execution_rationale: The transcript gives unusually specific end-to-end claims across several mathematical workflows and shared-state behaviors, but image inspection was unavailable and the packet does not provide a directly observed run.
execution_evidence: 179-second demo transcript covers graph construction, drag-dependent geometry, attention calculations, matrix shearing, history, and imported worksheet isolation.
Transcript explicitly distinguishes real arithmetic and computed results from canned animation.
About text describes a visible inspector, ledger, activity rail, and live app.
impact_rationale: It targets a clear educational limitation—an AI tutor that can discuss but not directly manipulate a learner's mathematical work—and addresses it with inspectable shared computation.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies student/tutor collaboration on a shared live math canvas.
Transcript frames the audience as learners needing manipulable, visual mathematics rather than explanations around a photograph or notebook.
About text spans late high school and early undergraduate mathematics.
creativity_rationale: The combination of collaborative tutoring, live dependent mathematical constructions, semantic handwriting/audit, and shared reversible agent state is a memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: About text combines semantic handwriting, geometry, matrix, attention, and theorem-boundary workflows.
Transcript demonstrates mapping attention weights to a geometric point and preserving dependencies during manipulation.
Shared one-history human/agent editing is a distinctive interaction premise.
usability_note: The described visible attribution, tool inspector, activity rail, and common undo support inspectability and recovery; direct usability is not visually verified.
red_flags: Native image inspection was rate-limited, so visual claims remain unverified.
Execution is based on claimed transcript and packaging rather than independent live observation.
standouts: Shared reducer and undo history across learner and tutor.
Deep mathematical examples rather than a superficial tool demo.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP indispensability, clear educational value, and unusually deep claimed execution make this a leading candidate despite unverified frames.

one_line: A task board where an agent can propose new WebMCP tools that require human approval before registration.
what_it_does: Combines task management with a constrained Tool Forge: proposed tools compose whitelisted read primitives, render for approval, and register only after a human UI click.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the product's central experiment: the agent extends the page's own structured tool surface, while human approval gates registration and execution. This is materially beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on proposing and testing brand-new WebMCP tools with approval-gated registration.
About text states registerTool fires only after a real UI click.
About text describes server rejection of writes unless confirmed true.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent concept and detailed safety model, but there is no submitted video, only one packaging screenshot, and no independent end-to-end evidence of tool proposal, approval, registration, and use.
execution_evidence: About text specifies three tool layers and an explicit approval flow.
Facts report a live demo link.
No video frame sheets or transcript submitted.
impact_rationale: Agent-generated task abstractions and approval-gated automation could help users manage repetitive work safely, though the audience and practical scope are less developed than the concept.
impact_evidence: About text identifies task boards and repetitive agent/UI interaction as the target problem.
Human approval is designed as a concrete safety boundary.
creativity_rationale: Self-extending, approval-gated WebMCP tooling is a notably original interaction model and a strong hackathon ambition.
creativity_evidence: Tool Forge proposes new tools rather than merely invoking fixed ones.
Whitelist composition and human registration approval create a distinctive constrained self-extension model.
usability_note: Approval cards and explicit gating are promising, but usability is not demonstrated in the packet.
red_flags: No video evidence.
Only one screenshot and truncated narrative limit execution verification.
standouts: Agent tool creation as a first-class product feature.
advance_reason: Exceptional originality and strong WebMCP leverage warrant advancement, while Stage 2 should verify the complete approval and registration loop.

one_line: A shift-handoff tool that lets agents analyze live notes and propose accountable follow-up without approving it.
what_it_does: Turns café closing notes into risk handoffs requiring an owner, deadline, and backup plan, with agent read/draft capabilities and human-only verification.
leverage_rationale: Structured live context and an intentionally absent approval tool create a meaningful safety and accountability boundary that general UI-driving agents cannot reliably guarantee.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says agents read live shift context and propose handoffs while only humans approve.
About text states no tool can mark a handoff verified.
About text reports an adversarial test where the agent refused to claim approval and audit log remained unchanged.
execution_rationale: The safety behavior and product flow are coherently described, but there is no video transcript, no gallery images, and no direct visual evidence in the packet.
execution_evidence: About text specifies risk ownership, deadlines, backup plans, audit behavior, and eight tools.
Facts report a live demo link.
Facts report zero gallery images and no video.
impact_rationale: The missing accountability between café shifts is concrete, with plausible operational value in preventing unresolved fridge, cash, and stock risks from being forgotten.
impact_evidence: About text gives specific café shift examples and multi-location context.
Required owner/deadline/backup plan directly addresses handoff failure.
creativity_rationale: Human-only approval enforced by tool absence is a strong safety framing, though shift handoff itself is a familiar workflow.
creativity_evidence: The 'missing hour' framing is clear.
No approval capability is structurally omitted rather than prompt-specified.
usability_note: The proposed risk checklist and audit trail support operational clarity; direct UI evidence is absent.
red_flags: No video or gallery evidence.
Execution relies almost entirely on self-reported description.
standouts: Adversarial approval test is a useful claimed validation.
Safety boundary is encoded in available tools.
advance_reason: Clear real-world problem and credible WebMCP safety delta; advance for verification despite thin evidence.

one_line: A live what-if decision simulator where humans and agents build, project, and compare scenarios together.
what_it_does: Lets an agent create and modify decision scenarios, project outcomes, and compare alternatives directly in a shared page model.
leverage_rationale: Structured scenario operations reduce spreadsheet copying and improve repeatability, but the stated workflow could largely be achieved through conventional UI or a general-purpose agent with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch lists create, modify, project, and compare operations on live scenarios.
About text emphasizes immediate visible changes to assumptions and consequences.
About text describes human constraints combined with agent modeling work.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent, but there are no video frames, transcript, public repository, or detailed demonstrated outputs in the packet; execution must be capped.
execution_evidence: Eight gallery images are reported, but no accessible visual verification was available.
Facts report a live demo link.
About text describes a complete intended workflow but not observed completion.
impact_rationale: Personal decision modeling is a real use case with identifiable value, but the packet does not establish a specific high-need audience or validated domain fit.
impact_evidence: About text identifies personal decision simulation and human/agent collaboration.
Visible assumptions and comparisons could improve informed decision-making.
creativity_rationale: Collaborative what-if modeling is a competent, useful synthesis with a modestly fresh agent interaction angle, but the concept is close to spreadsheet/decision-tool patterns.
creativity_evidence: Agent operates on live scenario objects rather than returning only prose advice.
Compare/project workflow is integrated into the same page.
usability_note: Shared visible assumptions and consequences are promising; direct usability is not verified.
red_flags: No video or transcript.
No public repository and thin packet detail.
standouts: Turns advice into editable, comparable scenarios rather than static text.
advance_reason: Plausible product with meaningful but not clearly distinctive WebMCP leverage; evidence is too thin relative to stronger packets.

one_line: A 3v3 pixel-art cat soccer game with a bounded semantic WebMCP sideline coach.
what_it_does: Provides human-played local matches with utility AI and coach tools for formations, styles, roles, tactical plays, and semantic orders without raw input or physics control.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes a semantic coaching layer while preserving simulation legality and player agency; raw UI automation cannot offer the same clean bounded command semantics as reliably.
leverage_evidence: Pitch identifies 23 WebMCP tools and a semantic sideline coach.
About text explicitly excludes raw key presses, coordinates, physics, and score changes.
About text describes causality trace, validation, local effects, and order outcomes.
execution_rationale: The description is detailed and covers state changes and edge cases, while frame sheets provide claimed product-motion evidence; however, visual contents could not be independently inspected.
execution_evidence: About text describes six original players with roles, skills, stamina, and live AI intent.
About text names handling for possession changes, goal resets, expired directives, and handoffs.
Facts report a live demo and three submitted frame sheets.
impact_rationale: The game offers entertainment and a legible experiment in safe agent participation, with a clear audience of players interested in AI-assisted play.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies an original playable arcade soccer game.
Coach opt-in and bounded tactics preserve human agency while adding strategic collaboration.
creativity_rationale: Semantic AI coaching inside a playable arcade match, with explicit agency and causality constraints, is a fresh and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent operates as sideline coach rather than direct avatar controller.
Bounded utility-AI effects and causality trace pursue the concept deeply.
usability_note: Opt-in states and causality tracing suggest a clear safe control model; direct frame inspection was unavailable.
red_flags: Video transcript is absent and images could not be inspected.
Game quality and actual playability remain claimed rather than observed.
standouts: Fun category handled without sacrificing WebMCP specificity.
advance_reason: Distinctive, well-scoped agent/game collaboration with credible leverage and enough claimed motion evidence to merit advancement.

one_line: A zero-trust support co-browsing platform using structured WebMCP proposals instead of screen sharing.
what_it_does: Streams declared tool state over edge WebSockets, lets representatives propose bounded fixes, and requires customer consent before local execution.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP changes the security and privacy model: support acts through typed tools on the customer's document rather than receiving DOM or screen access, with local consent gating execution.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes structured typed tool contracts registered on the document.
About text states representatives cannot touch DOM or execute actions unilaterally.
About text claims JSON protocol events replace video feeds and customer approval is required.
execution_rationale: The architecture and interaction are coherently specified, and frame sheets are submitted, but there is no transcript and visual inspection was unavailable; quantitative performance claims are unverified.
execution_evidence: About text specifies read-only state streaming, consent modal, bounded proposals, and no installation.
Facts report a live demo and public repository.
Three video frame sheets are listed but not independently viewable here.
impact_rationale: Privacy-preserving support is a concrete, consequential problem: avoiding exposure of payment data, passwords, and private inputs while retaining assistance has strong value for customers and support teams.
impact_evidence: About text identifies screen-sharing exposure risks.
Customer-controlled consent and local execution directly address that risk.
Low-bandwidth/no-install operation broadens practical usefulness.
creativity_rationale: Replacing intrusive co-browsing with a consented structured tool interface is a genuinely original interaction and architecture for support.
creativity_evidence: Zero-trust co-browsing framing is distinctive.
Kilobytes-instead-of-megabytes and document-confined execution pursue the model beyond a cosmetic integration.
usability_note: Explicit argument previews and customer approval should make support actions legible; direct UI verification is unavailable.
red_flags: Bandwidth figures and end-to-end behavior are self-reported.
Visual evidence could not be inspected due to vision rate limiting.
standouts: WebMCP is central to the product's trust boundary, not merely automation.
advance_reason: High-impact, technically distinctive privacy-preserving support model with major WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A cited funding-discovery agent for solo non-incorporated founders using live search and eligibility reasoning.
what_it_does: Searches SerpApi or grants.gov, filters to real returned opportunities, and presents cited discovery, eligibility, and readiness guidance.
leverage_rationale: Structured agent access can make live search and citation assembly convenient, but the core outcome is still achievable by a general-purpose agent using search and web pages; WebMCP is not shown as transformative.
leverage_evidence: Pitch cites live SerpApi search and Gemini reasoning.
About text describes a staged discovery-to-readiness workflow with source URLs.
No WebMCP-specific tool surface or agent-in-page collaboration is detailed in the packet excerpt.
execution_rationale: The demo is reported dead, there is no video or gallery evidence, and the packet offers only a narrative claim; this is thin evidence with a major live-availability concern.
execution_evidence: Facts report demo_alive=dead.
No video frame sheets or transcript.
About text claims live external APIs and citations but provides no observed output in the packet.
impact_rationale: Solo founders seeking non-dilutive funding are a specific audience with a real eligibility and discovery problem, and source-grounded filtering could provide credible value if operational.
impact_evidence: About text identifies solo non-incorporated founders and concrete grant-search friction.
Real opportunity numbers, agencies, close dates, and source links are specified.
creativity_rationale: The audience focus and discovery/eligibility/readiness pipeline add a useful angle to a familiar grant-search assistant, but the interaction model is not especially novel from the evidence.
creativity_evidence: Targets legal-entity eligibility rather than generic grant search.
Claims every recommendation is grounded in returned live results.
usability_note: A staged workflow could be useful, but the reported dead demo prevents confidence in the user experience.
red_flags: Demo is reported dead.
No visual or video evidence.
External API and citation behavior are unverified.
advance_reason: Real problem and plausible value, but dead demo and absent execution evidence make it ineligible/too uncertain for advancement.

one_line: A print-shopping assistant that translates natural-language needs into a reviewed real-shop print setup.
what_it_does: Reads documents and print context, proposes price/readability/eco plans from shop rates, applies the selected setup, and stops before checkout payment.
leverage_rationale: Typed print context, document-aware plan generation, live shop comparison, and safe preparation address a settings-heavy workflow with precision; the explicit absence of order/payment tools makes the boundary meaningful.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says the agent handles the whole setup but user presses pay.
About text lists nine imperative WebMCP tools for context, plans, comparison, preparation, status, and checkout review.
About text explicitly states there is no place_order or pay_order tool.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete prepare-to-checkout flow and submits three frame sheets, but no transcript is available and visual inspection was unavailable.
execution_evidence: About text gives four plan types, real sheet counts, estimated prices, trade-offs, shop capabilities, and ETA.
Facts report a live demo and two gallery images plus three frame sheets.
Claimed test asserts dangerous order/payment tools do not exist.
impact_rationale: People needing printing under time and cost constraints face genuinely confusing technical settings; natural-language translation and readability trade-offs directly address the problem.
impact_evidence: About text gives concrete exam-tomorrow printing scenario.
Plans compare cost, speed, readability, and eco trade-offs at real nearby shops.
creativity_rationale: The product makes the natural-language-to-physical-print translation the central interaction and treats human payment control as a deliberate product boundary.
creativity_evidence: Print configuration is reframed around user goals rather than duplex/pages-per-sheet jargon.
Agent changes the draft being viewed while preserving user confirmation for irreversible steps.
usability_note: Goal-based plans and human-controlled checkout are strong usability choices; direct visual verification is unavailable.
red_flags: No video transcript and images could not be inspected.
Live shop rates/ETAs are claimed, not independently verified.
standouts: Clear translation from user goals to print settings and trade-offs.
advance_reason: Strong concrete user pain, credible WebMCP leverage, and careful safety boundary make this advancement-worthy.

one_line: An accessibility-first task board where human focus establishes the target and an agent performs safe semantic edits.
what_it_does: Uses Focus Relay to connect keyboard or assistive-input focus to atomic card updates, receipts, conflict checks, and undo.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP binds ephemeral human-established page context to precise structured agent actions, eliminating repeated target identification and fragile pointer manipulation in a way general UI automation cannot match reliably.
leverage_evidence: Pitch identifies users unable to reliably drag cards or complete dense forms.
Transcript states the human establishes focus and WebMCP resolves the current target unambiguously.
About text describes atomic multi-field update, before/after receipt, conflict-safe refusal, and one-intent undo.
execution_rationale: The 70-second transcript demonstrates a broad coherent workflow from live board read/search through atomic edits, creation, assignment, dates, priority, and undo; frame sheets add claimed motion evidence, though visuals could not be inspected.
execution_evidence: Transcript enumerates live board summary, exact card search, atomic update, card creation, semantic movement, editing, assignment, dates, priority, and undo.
About text describes normal workflow preservation and refusal to overwrite newer human changes.
Facts report public repository, live demo, video, and two gallery images.
impact_rationale: It addresses a significant accessibility barrier in a common task-board workflow for keyboard, switch-control, and eye-gaze users, while also reducing friction for everyone.
impact_evidence: About text names assistive-input users and dense controls as the target problem.
Focus Relay lets a person establish intent with their available input while the agent handles manipulation.
Visible receipts and recovery improve accountability.
creativity_rationale: Focus Relay—a human sets context through focus and an agent safely executes semantic multi-field work—is a novel, memorable interaction model with deep follow-through.
creativity_evidence: The live focused target is distinct from ordinary ID-based APIs or screen automation.
Conflict-safe checks and atomic undo extend the concept beyond a convenience shortcut.
usability_note: The focus-first model, visible receipt, and atomic undo are promising accessibility and recovery affordances; direct frame inspection was unavailable.
red_flags: Frame images could not be inspected due to vision rate limiting.
Execution remains claimed rather than independently observed.
standouts: Human focus context plus agent execution is an excellent WebMCP fit.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: transformative leverage, high concrete impact, and a distinctive interaction model supported by a detailed demo transcript.

one_line: A local-first WebMCP debugger for NPC beliefs, rumor provenance, and canon-change fallout in narrative games.
what_it_does: Lets narrative developers search beliefs, trace rumors, evaluate conditions, stage edits, and apply page-reviewed patches with deterministic projections and receipts.
leverage_rationale: Structured page tools expose live narrative state and revision-bound review/apply semantics; the agent can reason over precise provenance and condition projections without unsafe direct world mutation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch identifies a WebMCP debugger with five narrow site tools.
About text says deterministic TypeScript, not the model, calculates beliefs, provenance, projections, and validity.
About text states early Apply changes no data and later commits only page-approved operations.
execution_rationale: The narrative gives a specific reproducible 1→1→0 debugging workflow and detailed state semantics, with three submitted frame sheets, but no transcript and no direct visual inspection.
execution_evidence: About text describes objective canon vs belief, rumor distortion, two-axis condition results, and revision/fingerprint-bound review.
The 1→1→0 example demonstrates a nontrivial regression and subsequent repair.
Facts report live demo, public repository, and three frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Branching-game developers have a real debugging problem where canon changes silently break quest conditions and belief provenance; the tool directly targets that niche.
impact_evidence: About text identifies branching narrative developers and concrete hidden-regression failure modes.
Preserving incorrect beliefs and provenance rather than deleting them supports narrative integrity.
creativity_rationale: NPC belief provenance, rumor distortion chains, and canon-change fallout are an unusually specific and original debugging concept, pursued with strong interaction depth.
creativity_evidence: The tool treats beliefs, rumors, conditions, and repair projections as inspectable linked state.
The 1→1→0 demonstration makes a subtle narrative regression legible.
Page-reviewed patches and deterministic projections are distinctive safeguards.
usability_note: The two-axis diagnostics and reviewed patches suggest strong developer legibility; direct UI evidence is unavailable.
red_flags: No video transcript and images could not be inspected.
Specialized workflow may need live verification for completeness.
standouts: Excellent domain specificity and memorable 1→1→0 debugging story.
Preserves provenance and incorrect beliefs instead of flattening narrative state.
advance_reason: Highly original, credible developer niche with meaningful structured-state leverage and a concrete demonstrated debugging model.
